projects.title: MetaExtract
projects.tagline: Structured data from documents that never come in the same format twice
projects.proofSummary: Takes a real production mess (different formats, different layouts, noisy scans) and turns it into structured, reviewable output.
projects.demonstrates: How I design modular extraction systems that handle real document variability while staying operable for teams.
projects.description: A modular extraction system built to pull structured data from PDFs, scanned images, and documents that never come in the same format twice. Designed for document-heavy healthcare operations where the inputs are messy and the outputs need to be reliable.
projects.problem: Organizations sit on thousands of documents (invoices, contracts, medical records, reports) that each arrive in a different layout, format, and quality level. Getting structured data out of them means either massive manual effort or brittle one-off scripts that break when the next batch looks different.
projects.approach: Built a FastAPI backend with a pluggable parser architecture: each document type gets its own parser combining layout heuristics, regex patterns, and ML classification. Results normalize into a unified schema. Async job queue handles batch runs. React dashboard gives operations visibility into queue status and extraction quality.
projects.result: Modular extraction system handling heterogeneous document workflows in healthcare operations.

technicalDepth.architecture: Modular FastAPI backend with pluggable parsers per document type. Async job queue for batch processing. PostgreSQL for metadata storage, Redis for caching.
technicalDepth.ocrPipeline: Tesseract OCR with custom preprocessing (deskewing, denoising, contrast normalization). Layout analysis using heuristic + ML-based region detection.
technicalDepth.normalization: Unified schema mapping variations to standardized outputs. Confidence scoring per field with fallback rules.
technicalDepth.performance: Designed for batch processing of heterogeneous document sets. Single-page extraction completes in a few seconds on standard hardware.
technicalDepth.integration: REST API with webhook callbacks. React dashboard for monitoring queue status and reviewing extraction accuracy.

outcomes: Processes highly variable semantic structures from heterogeneous document formats
Reduced manual data entry for core healthcare document workflows
Confidence scoring enables human review queue prioritization
projects.ownership: Owned system design and implementation end-to-end: extraction pipeline, normalization logic, API layer, and operator-facing monitoring flow.
constraints: Heterogeneous source documents with inconsistent layouts and noisy scans
Need for usable confidence scores to support human review queues
Production reliability requirements in document-heavy healthcare operations
tradeoffs: Used a hybrid rules + ML approach instead of model-only extraction to keep outputs debuggable and reliable by field type
Prioritized high-confidence core fields first, then expanded long-tail field coverage incrementally
whatChanged: Manual extraction and copy-paste became API-backed structured outputs
Review teams moved from full-document checking to confidence-prioritized exception review
artifacts: Queue-level extraction status view for operations
Per-field confidence and normalization trace for reviewer decisions
Unified output schema mapping thousands of field variants

projects.title: SignKit
projects.tagline: Signature extraction and PDF signing, built into one desktop workflow
projects.proofSummary: Went from identifying a workflow pain point to shipping a paid product with real users. Not a demo, not a side project. A commercial tool people pay for.
projects.demonstrates: How I take a workflow pain point from idea to paid product with real usage and operational constraints.
projects.description: A commercial desktop application for signature extraction and PDF document processing. Handles batch document workflows for legal and financial teams. Built from idea to paid product, including extraction, signing, billing, and cross-platform distribution.
projects.problem: Legal and financial teams process thousands of signed documents. The existing workflow means juggling separate tools for extraction, signing, and organization. Nobody wants three apps for what should be one flow.
projects.approach: PySide6 cross-platform desktop app with FastAPI backend. OpenCV-based signature extraction using morphological operations. PDF signing with embedded certificate support. PostgreSQL for document metadata and user management. Stripe for billing, license keys, and trial flow.
projects.result: Paid product with early customer validation. Extraction, signing, billing, and distribution shipped end-to-end.

technicalDepth.cvPipeline: OpenCV morphological operations (dilation, erosion, contour detection) to isolate signature regions. Handles handwritten signatures on scanned documents, photos, and mixed backgrounds.
technicalDepth.backend: FastAPI with async document processing. PostgreSQL for user accounts, document metadata, and audit trails.
technicalDepth.signing: PDF signing with embedded certificate chains. Signature appearance customization. Batch signing for multi-document workflows.
technicalDepth.monetization: Stripe integration for subscription billing. License key validation. Trial mode with full feature access for 14 days.
technicalDepth.distribution: Cross-platform builds for Windows and macOS. Code-signed binaries. Auto-updater integration.

outcomes: Paid product with early customer validation
Signature extraction handles clean and degraded scanned documents
Batch processing workflows for legal and financial teams
Cross-platform distribution (Windows/macOS) with code signing and auto-update
projects.ownership: Owned product and build from idea to paid release: desktop UX, extraction/signing pipeline, billing integration, packaging, and shipping workflow.
constraints: Needed both signature extraction and signing in one operational flow, not separate tools
Cross-platform distribution and update reliability for non-technical end users
Accuracy requirements on imperfect scanned documents
tradeoffs: Chose desktop-first workflow (PySide6) for local file-heavy operations instead of web-only upload flow
Focused initial release on core extraction + signing reliability before broader template and collaboration features
whatChanged: Replaced fragmented manual signing process with a single structured workflow
Moved from prototype utility to paid product with licensing and subscription flow
artifacts: Batch signing queue with status tracking
Signature region extraction pipeline and confidence checks

projects.title: EchoPanel
projects.tagline: Record a meeting, find what was said later
projects.proofRole: Platform breadth + real product use case
projects.proofSummary: Combines native macOS UX, transcription, and local-first retrieval into one workflow. Not three separate tools duct-taped together.
projects.demonstrates: How I combine product workflow design with technical implementation to build practical local-first systems.
projects.description: A native macOS menu bar app that captures meeting audio, transcribes it, and makes the transcript searchable after the fact. The whole point: you hit record, forget about it, then search the transcript when you need to find what was actually said.
projects.problem: People in meetings, interviews, and research sessions spend more time replaying recordings to find a specific moment than they spent in the meeting itself. Existing tools either dump raw audio files, require cloud uploads, or make searching painful.
projects.approach: Swift menu bar app using AVFoundation for audio capture. FastAPI backend with Whisper for transcription. SQLite with full-text search for local transcript storage. Global hotkey so recording starts in one tap. Minimal UI, maximum utility.
projects.result: Local-first meeting capture with transcription and full-text search across all recordings.

technicalDepth.audioCapture: AVFoundation audio engine with custom audio buffer management. Captures system audio via CoreAudio APIs. Streaming to backend for near-real-time processing.
technicalDepth.transcription: Whisper model for on-device transcription. Chunked processing for live sessions. Speaker diarization experiments.
technicalDepth.storage: SQLite with FTS5 for full-text search. Local-first architecture with export options (SRT, TXT, JSON).
technicalDepth.ux: Menu bar widget with global hotkey. Minimal UI: record button, status indicator, transcript view. Searchable history with timestamp navigation.
technicalDepth.integration: FastAPI backend for optional processing. WebSocket streaming for live transcription preview.

outcomes: Native macOS UX with global hotkey activation
On-device transcription with Whisper on Apple Silicon
Local-first storage with full-text search across all transcripts
Export formats: SRT, plain text, structured JSON
projects.ownership: Owned prototype architecture and implementation across native app layer, transcription pipeline integration, and local-first transcript retrieval flow.
constraints: Needed low-friction capture from a menu bar workflow, not a heavy standalone app
Transcription latency had to stay acceptable for near-real-time feedback
Local-first storage and search for privacy-sensitive usage
tradeoffs: Prioritized reliable capture + searchable transcript history over broad collaboration features
Used practical chunked processing strategy to balance speed and accuracy during live sessions
whatChanged: Audio capture and transcript retrieval moved from ad-hoc tools to one integrated flow
Users could search transcript history by content and timestamp instead of replaying long recordings
artifacts: Menu bar recorder with status and quick actions

projects.title: PhotoSearch
projects.tagline: Search your photos by describing what is in them
projects.proofSummary: Turns a folder of photos into a searchable library. You describe what you are looking for and it finds it, locally.
projects.demonstrates: How I build local-first products where natural language retrieval, clustering, and review workflows work together.
projects.description: A local-first media search workstation. Instead of browsing by folder or filename, you describe what you are looking for and the system finds matching photos. Supports natural language queries, metadata exploration, and people clustering as one layer of the workflow.
projects.problem: Large photo libraries become unmanageable with folders and filenames. You know the photo you want but you can not find it. Existing tools either require cloud uploads or do not understand what is actually in the image.
projects.approach: FastAPI + LanceDB backend with CLIP-based semantic retrieval. Tauri + React desktop client for local-first workflow. People clustering as a supporting feature, not the main story. Incremental indexing so large libraries do not require a full rebuild every time.
projects.result: Local-first media search workstation with natural language retrieval, metadata workflows, and people clustering.

technicalDepth.architecture: FastAPI service layer with separate indexing and query paths. LanceDB stores embeddings; desktop client uses Tauri + React for local workflow UX.
technicalDepth.performance: Incremental indexing for large libraries. Semantic queries return results quickly on indexed collections.
technicalDepth.integration: Combined CLIP semantic retrieval with person clustering and metadata workflows to support concept, context, and identity-oriented review paths.

outcomes: Natural language retrieval across local photo libraries
Face clustering for people-centric queries without manual tagging
Desktop workflow that unifies indexing, search, and review in one tool
projects.ownership: Owned full-stack implementation of indexing, natural-language retrieval, metadata flows, and desktop workflow orchestration.
constraints: Large local libraries with mixed quality metadata and inconsistent naming
Desktop-first experience that can handle long indexing runs
Balancing semantic relevance, people clustering quality, and query latency
tradeoffs: Prioritized local workstation workflow and retrieval quality over cloud sync features in early versions
Shipped semantic retrieval + clustering workflow before broader media management capabilities
whatChanged: Browsing by folders and filenames shifted to concept-driven retrieval
People-centric queries became practical via face clustering instead of manual tagging
artifacts: Indexing status workflow for large photo libraries
Semantic query interface with ranked result grid
Face cluster review and merge flow

projects.title: model-lab

projects.proofSummary: Built the infrastructure to compare models fairly: same harness, same data, same metrics. The kind of discipline that matters before deployment decisions.
projects.description: A systematic evaluation workbench for audio AI models (ASR, diarization, related pipelines). Designed to answer a specific question: which model should we actually deploy, given our accuracy, speed, cost, and hardware constraints?
projects.problem: Choosing the right audio AI model means comparing across accuracy, speed, cost, and hardware. Running a few informal tests is not enough to make a deployment decision. Teams need infrastructure to evaluate with data.
projects.approach: Built as a repeatable evaluation framework with shared harness, identical metrics, and automated comparison dashboards. Tested across Apple Silicon MPS, NVIDIA CUDA, and CPU. Produced readiness grades for Whisper variants and LFM2.5-Audio.
projects.result: Evaluation harness for ASR pipeline comparison with repeatable runs, scorecards, and hardware-aware findings.

process.title: Discovery
process.description: We get clear on the problem, the constraints, the users, and what a useful first version actually needs to do.

process.title: Scope
process.description: I turn that into a concrete scope with deliverables, timeline, and clear boundaries.

process.title: Build
process.description: I work in short milestones so progress is visible early. The goal is working solutions, not long status cycles.

process.title: Handoff
process.description: You get something usable, documented, and understandable, with a short support window to close the loop properly.

faq.question: What is the smallest scope you take?
faq.answer: Usually something with a clear workflow, a real user need, and a narrow first version that can be built in weeks rather than months.

faq.question: What if the idea is still vague?
faq.answer: That is fine as long as there is a real problem underneath it. Part of the early work is turning a vague request into a tighter scope.

faq.question: Do you work with existing teams?
faq.answer: Yes. That is often the best setup. I can plug into an existing product, engineering, or operations context and help move a specific build forward.

faq.question: What does a typical week look like?
faq.answer: Clear milestone, visible progress, and working output. I prefer short feedback loops over long reporting cycles.

faq.question: Do you handle deployment?
faq.answer: Yes. Docker containers, CI/CD pipelines, and monitoring are included in prototype and automation engagements. I do not hand off and say call someone else to deploy.
